global.name: Mont Saint-Michel
global.summary: Mont Saint-Michel is arguably one of Europe’s strongest defensive positions: a tidal island with medieval walls, steep approaches, elevated fighting positions, and commanding visibility across the bay. Its real survival test is not whether zombies can storm the mount; it is whether the people inside can solve food, freshwater, and crowd-control problems once mainland supply chains fail.

global.name: Machu Picchu
global.summary: Machu Picchu offers excellent terrain defense and controlled approach lines, but limited productive capacity prevents large, permanent survival communities.

global.name: Simien Mountains
global.summary: The Simien Mountains are a naturally defensible high-altitude stronghold, where sheer cliffs, limited access routes, and extreme isolation significantly reduce external threat pressure. However, that same isolation severely limits long-term survivability, with constrained food production, harsh living conditions, and difficult resupply. Over time, the balance shifts from protection to restriction, making it better suited to short-term refuge than permanent settlement.

global.name: Carcassonne
global.summary: Carcassonne is a premier fortified shell with layered walls and command depth; what kills you here is sustainment fatigue behind intact defenses.

global.name: Faroe Islands
global.summary: Faroe is one of Europe's strongest isolation plays, but what kills you here is maritime bottleneck failure when storms, fuel limits, and fleet wear cut food and medical imports.

global.name: Hilltop Fort Rajasthan
global.summary: A Rajasthan hill fort is a classic high-control stronghold with excellent wall geometry, but water and heat stress define whether it thrives or slowly fails.

global.name: Socotra Island
global.summary: Socotra gives outstanding separation from collapse corridors, but what kills you here is maritime supply fracture: once sea links fail, medicine, tools, and replacement goods run out faster than local systems can adapt.

global.name: Fiji Islands
global.summary: Fiji balances isolation and livability better than most island options, but cyclone and maritime dependence cap reliability.

global.name: Krak des Chevaliers
global.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a premier fortress for holding ground, but what kills you here is siege economics: ammunition, medicine, and calories run out long before the walls meaningfully fail.

global.name: Palawan
global.summary: Palawan is a large island system that balances isolation, defensibility, and resource diversity. It works when distributed settlements and logistics are coordinated at island-wide scale. You die when governance fractures and shipping disruption desynchronizes regional supply.

global.name: Kodiak Island
global.summary: Kodiak is a high-isolation island with credible wild-resource potential, but its dominant failure mode is climate-logistics attrition: severe weather and seasonal bottlenecks steadily erode throughput, maintenance, and medical resilience.

global.name: Matmata Underground Dwellings
global.summary: Matmata offers a strong concealment-defense package with naturally insulated subterranean housing and manageable access points. Its core trade-off is protected living space versus limited scale and external dependence for growth.

global.name: Rice Terrace Highlands
global.summary: Rice Terrace Highlands are elevated agrarian settlements with built-in food potential. They work by combining controllable approach routes with reliable staple production systems. You die when irrigation, labor coordination, or slope access fails during stress cycles.

global.name: Sigiriya
global.summary: Sigiriya offers rare rock-fortress defensibility and visibility, but constrained top-plateau capacity limits how long a group can live there without strong external support.

global.name: Zanzibar Island
global.summary: Zanzibar balances meaningful island separation with established settlement infrastructure, making it a credible medium-to-long-term refuge if governance and resource management remain coherent. Its challenge is that it is populated and close enough to mainland dynamics to face persistent pressure.

global.name: Burlington Bunker
global.summary: Burlington is exceptionally hard to breach in the opening phase; what kills you here is closed-system decay once consumables, maintenance, or governance slip.

global.name: Cappadocia Highlands
global.summary: Cappadocia’s broken terrain and concealment options make it a strong defensive refuge, but what kills you here is water-and-agriculture throughput: dispersed hideouts can outlast attacks, not prolonged scarcity.

global.name: Coober Pedy Underground Settlement
global.summary: Coober Pedy is one of the few desert sites where underground habitation is already proven, but long-term success is limited by hard water and logistics ceilings.

global.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
global.summary: Derinkuyu is an elite hide-and-hold refuge, but what kills you here is subterranean throughput collapse: ventilation, waste handling, and calorie flow fail before defenses do.

global.name: Gotland
global.summary: Gotland is a robust island option with workable infrastructure, but what kills you here is coastline overextension: too many access points for too few defenders over time.

global.name: Hanle Observatory
global.summary: Hanle Observatory is an isolation-dominant survival option with low encounter pressure, but extreme altitude and remoteness impose severe physiological and logistics penalties.

global.name: Jeju Island
global.summary: Jeju is a strong island refuge with usable farmland, water access, and natural maritime separation from mainland spillover. What kills you here is maritime choke failure: if ports and fuel fail, an island-scale population can out-consume local capacity.

global.name: Kargil War Bunkers
global.summary: Kargil War Bunkers are military-hardened high-altitude positions designed to resist assault. They work by combining strong fortification with terrain that channels approaches. You die when cold-weather fuel, medical, and resupply throughput collapses before defenses do.

global.name: Mount Huashan
global.summary: Mount Huashan is an elite defensive perch with severe access control and strong natural isolation. The decisive trade-off is near-unmatched protection versus chronic logistical fragility.

global.name: Siwa Oasis
global.summary: Siwa Oasis is one of the more credible long-horizon refuges in the region, but what kills you here is water-system fragility: contamination, overdraw, or pump failure can collapse the settlement’s carrying capacity.

global.name: Aït Benhaddou
global.summary: Aït Benhaddou is a strong niche base: its fortified settlement form and relative isolation support controlled defense and lower immediate pressure. Its long-term ceiling is set by arid constraints, where limited water and food capacity become the decisive bottleneck.

global.name: Galápagos Islands
global.summary: Galápagos has extreme isolation and low random threat traffic, but what kills you here is supply collapse once imported essentials stop.

global.name: Hallstatt
global.summary: Hallstatt combines constrained access with strong local livability, making it one of the better balanced settlement options. What kills you here is chokepoint failure that traps residents against terrain.

global.name: Iwo Jima Underground Bunkers
global.summary: Iwo Jima’s bunker network is exceptionally hard to assault and highly isolated, but it is austere and resource-poor. What kills you here is life-support collapse underground: water, ventilation, and medical limits outrun defensive advantages.

global.name: Malbork Castle
global.summary: Malbork provides exceptional masonry defense and layered gates, but it sits in a reachable lowland region. What kills you here is siege attrition: repeated encirclement and supply disruption grind down even a strong fortress.

global.name: Telluride
global.summary: Mountain terrain and manageable scale make Telluride a credible holdout if you prepare for winter logistics.

global.name: Visby
global.summary: Visby is a balanced walled island town, but what kills you here is population-and-water strain if too many survivors concentrate behind finite historic defenses.

global.name: Île d’Yeu
global.summary: Île d’Yeu is a balanced island refuge with useful separation and livable conditions, but it lacks deep strategic depth. What kills you here is slow resource depletion under prolonged isolation.

global.name: Fasil Ghebbi
global.summary: Fasil Ghebbi is a fortified royal compound with thick masonry, layered courtyards, and strong internal control, giving it above-average defensive potential in an inland setting. It is more balanced than many heritage landmarks, but long-term survival still depends on building reliable food, water, and medical systems beyond the walls.

global.name: Lindisfarne
global.summary: A tidal island with natural separation, limited access windows, and a defensible settlement pattern. It works well for a disciplined small group, but tide dependency and resource limits cap long-term resilience.

global.name: Predjama Castle
global.summary: Predjama is a superb cliff fortress with choke-point control, but fortress geometry does not make food or medicine. What kills you here is siege starvation: you can deny entry for a long time and still lose to depletion.

global.name: Qeshm Island
global.summary: Qeshm offers valuable island separation and room for mixed subsistence, but what kills you here is control dilution: the island is large enough that fragmented authority invites persistent infiltration and internal conflict.

global.name: Rocamadour
global.summary: Rocamadour balances cliffside defense with workable rural linkage; what kills you here is exceeding carrying capacity and overloading water/sanitation systems.

global.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge Cliffs
global.summary: Tiger Leaping Gorge offers extraordinary terrain defense and low approach density, but daily survival is constrained by space and supply movement. The central trade-off is tactical dominance versus unworkable sustainment at scale.

global.name: Tiger’s Nest Monastery
global.summary: Tiger’s Nest is an extreme cliffside redoubt with elite access denial, but its tiny carrying capacity and severe logistics ceiling cap long-term survival.

global.name: Alcatraz Island
global.summary: Alcatraz buys strong early security through water separation and choke-point access, but the decisive failure mode is supply starvation: once boat fuel, food inflow, and repair parts lapse, the island becomes a sealed deficit zone.

global.name: Banda Neira
global.summary: A small island settlement with strong maritime separation, historic fortifications, and access to coastal resources. It works best as a low-profile island refuge, but limited scale and supply dependence cap long-term resilience.

global.name: Caerphilly Castle
global.summary: A large moated castle with strong defensive design and layered barriers. It is one of the stronger historic fortifications, but modern exposure and limited self-sufficiency keep it from elite status.

global.name: Himeji Castle
global.summary: Himeji Castle delivers high-quality fortress geometry and controlled internal defense, but its urban context limits long-term security. The key trade-off is superb structure versus low isolation.

global.name: Masada
global.summary: Masada is brutally hard to assault, but what kills you here is plateau logistics: water, heat management, and medical throughput collapse before attackers can force entry.

global.name: Mesa Verde
global.summary: Mesa Verde offers strong terrain defense, but what kills you here is carrying-capacity mismatch: protected positions can hold people, yet arable throughput and water logistics limit long-run population support.

global.name: Olavsvern Naval Base
global.summary: A hardened underground naval base with strong concealment and protected infrastructure. However, confined systems, external supply needs, and limited scalability restrict long-term survival.

global.name: St Kilda
global.summary: An extremely remote island archipelago with exceptional isolation and low external threat pressure. Its weakness is sustainment: weather, landing difficulty, and limited resources make survival fragile over time.

global.name: Nagurskoye Air Base
global.summary: A remote Arctic military airbase with controlled access and strong strategic positioning. However, extreme climate, visibility, and dependence on supply chains reduce independent survivability.

global.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
global.summary: A purpose-built tunnel network with concealment, restricted access, and strong defensive history. It is highly effective for short-term evasion, but confinement, ventilation, and resource limits make permanent survival difficult.

global.name: Fort George
global.summary: A purpose-built coastal military fort with strong walls, controlled access, and organised internal space. It has real defensive value, but exposure and reliance on external supplies limit long-term independence.

global.name: Fort Jefferson
global.summary: Fort Jefferson is an exceptional sea-fortress with clear defensive geometry and extreme stand-off distance, but its dominant failure mode is water-energy fragility: if desalination and fuel chains degrade, habitability collapses quickly.

global.name: HM Prison Dartmoor
global.summary: A remote prison complex with secure walls, controlled movement, and strong internal containment. It offers a credible short-term defensive shell, but harsh exposure and limited self-sufficiency constrain long-term survival.

global.name: Ha Long Bay Cliffs
global.summary: Ha Long Bay cliffs are a terrain-fragmented coastal redoubt of islands and vertical rock. It works by forcing movement through predictable maritime channels and narrow landing points. You die when weather or boat degradation cuts mobility and resupply between sectors.

global.name: Hue Citadel
global.summary: Hue Citadel is a fortified urban compound with layered walls and controlled gates. It works as a short-to-medium defensive enclave where geometry slows penetration. You die when siege pressure outlasts external food, fuel, and medical inflows.

global.name: Suomenlinna Fortress
global.summary: Suomenlinna has real island-fortress defensive logic, but it is tied to nearby urban waters and maritime supply. What kills you here is blockade-driven depletion when fuel, food, and treatment capacity cannot be replenished.

global.name: Clovelly
global.summary: A steep coastal village with constrained access routes, natural defensibility, and small-scale shelter. It is viable as a compact refuge, but limited expansion, coastal exposure, and supply dependence restrict long-term survival.

global.name: Edinburgh Castle
global.summary: A highly defensible urban castle on elevated rock, with strong visibility and controlled approaches. It is excellent as a symbolic redoubt, but urban exposure and limited sustainability reduce long-term value.

global.name: Kibber Village
global.summary: Kibber is a high-altitude remote village that trades accessibility for security. It works through isolation, narrow approaches, and existing community housing for organized routines. You die when winter isolation, fuel gaps, or delayed medical care compound faster than recovery.

global.name: Komodo Island
global.summary: Komodo is a highly isolated island refuge with strong separation from mainland pressure. It works by limiting approach routes and maintaining disciplined low-population maritime living. You die when freshwater constraints and sea-logistics disruption trigger cascading shortages.

global.name: Lakshadweep
global.summary: Lakshadweep is a distributed island-chain refuge where sea separation reduces routine contact and gives strong early warning. It works when multiple islands coordinate boats, storage, and rationing as one system. You die when maritime links or freshwater discipline fail and each island is stranded alone.

global.name: McMurdo Station
global.summary: A large Antarctic research station with infrastructure, shelter, and operational capacity. However, harsh conditions and dependence on supply chains limit true long-term independence.

global.name: Table Mountain Plateau
global.summary: Table Mountain Plateau is a highly defensible elevated position with steep cliffs, strong visibility, and usable space on top. However, its direct proximity to Cape Town, multiple access routes, and high visibility make it far less secure than more remote mountain strongholds. It is better suited to short-term defence and staging than long-term isolation.

global.name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
global.summary: An extremely isolated scientific station with controlled infrastructure and almost no external threat pressure. However, total dependence on life-support systems and resupply makes long-term independence impossible.

global.name: Longyearbyen
global.summary: A remote Arctic settlement with strong isolation, infrastructure, and controlled access. However, extreme climate and supply-chain reliance constrain long-term resilience.

global.name: Petra
global.summary: Petra offers strong chokepoints and concealment in stone corridors, but what kills you here is water dependency: once stored supply and nearby sources are contested, defensive geometry cannot feed or hydrate a population.

global.name: San Felipe Fortress
global.summary: San Felipe combines historical fortification advantages with moderate operating feasibility, but limited local throughput caps long-term resilience.

global.name: Danum Valley Field Centre
global.summary: Danum Valley Field Centre is a remote jungle refuge with low-contact signature advantages. It works for small trained groups that can run strict field medicine and maintenance routines. You die when treatable illness, injury, or equipment failure outpaces evacuation and repair.

global.name: Pine Gap Facility
global.summary: Extreme remoteness and hardened controls are offset by acute system dependency and top-tier strategic exposure.

global.name: Al Udeid Air Base
global.summary: Al Udeid provides one of the best ready-made defense envelopes in the region, but what kills you here is signature load: major airbase visibility attracts sustained external pressure and drains supplies.

global.name: Elmina Castle
global.summary: Elmina Castle is a heavily fortified coastal stronghold with thick walls, controlled internal spaces, and clear defensive advantages. However, its position within a populated coastal town and direct access from land and sea significantly reduce its long-term viability, making it better suited to temporary defence than sustained survival.

global.name: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base
global.summary: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base is a military command compound with strong tactical security. It works through hardened access control, organized response, and maritime support infrastructure. You die when prolonged contest burns fuel, parts, and readiness faster than resupply.

global.name: Okinawa
global.summary: Okinawa offers meaningful island separation and workable living conditions, but dense infrastructure and strategic visibility increase contest pressure. What kills you here is competition over ports, fuel, and transport hubs that fractures island stability.

global.name: Amazon Tall Tower Observatory
global.summary: ATTO offers deep-rainforest isolation and strong natural resource potential, but terrain, disease burden, and mobility constraints make control and continuity difficult.

global.name: Banlung
global.summary: A remote inland town with surrounding terrain, forest cover, and regional resource access. It offers more livability than a pure wilderness refuge, but weak defensibility and difficult logistics limit its ceiling.

global.name: Guantanamo Bay
global.summary: Guantanamo offers strong perimeter control and organized facilities, yet the dominant failure mode is geopolitical encirclement: prolonged dependence on maritime logistics and contested sovereignty can choke continuity even before direct breach.

global.name: Table Rock Plateau
global.summary: Table Rock is a serviceable elevated fallback, but what kills you here is perimeter dilution: broad approach arcs and limited concealment stretch defenders until incidents become constant.

global.name: Blue Mountains Cliffs
global.summary: Excellent terrain defense and standoff distance, with sustainment limited by wildfire and infrastructure thinness.

global.name: Kimberley Big Hole & Mining Complex
global.summary: The Kimberley Big Hole offers strong terrain-based defensibility, but it is a dangerous bowl if exits, water access, or supply routes fail. It works as a hard-to-storm holdout early on, yet can quickly become a trap once core lifelines are cut.

global.name: Maginot Line Bunkers
global.summary: The Maginot bunkers are elite for hard protection but poor at independent endurance. What kills you here is subsystem failure underground: air, water, power, and sanitation.

global.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
global.summary: Neuschwanstein offers strong terrain-assisted defense and visibility; what kills you here is logistics drag from a symbolic site that cannot feed itself.

global.name: Shirakawa-go
global.summary: Shirakawa-go benefits from mountain remoteness and small-settlement cohesion, but severe winters and limited redundancy constrain endurance. What kills you here is winter logistics failure: heat, medicine, and mobility collapse before threats do.

global.name: Tambopata Research Center
global.summary: Tambopata gives concealment and food potential in deep jungle, but what kills you here is untreated injury or infection far from reliable care.

global.name: Hutchinson Salt Storage Caverns
global.summary: Hutchinson salt caverns provide excellent blast/weather protection and concealment, yet the single dominant failure mode is ventilation-power dependency: lose airflow and pumping reliability, and the underground advantage becomes a liability.

global.name: The Roaches
global.summary: A rocky elevated ridge with natural defensibility, visibility, and difficult approaches. It works as a temporary fallback point, but exposure and lack of infrastructure make it unsuitable for long-term occupation.

global.name: Camp Century Ice Tunnels
global.summary: Camp Century is exceptionally hard to reach and hard to assault, but it fails as a settlement because the environment itself destroys long-term habitability.

global.name: Waw an Namus Cave System
global.summary: Waw an Namus is one of the hardest places to reach, which dramatically lowers threat pressure. The same isolation becomes the fatal weakness because survival systems are almost entirely import-dependent.

global.name: Ajanta Caves
global.summary: Ajanta Caves are a hardened cave shelter system with strong choke-point defense. It works for short protected occupancy because rock-cut access geometry lowers breach risk. You die when confinement-driven sanitation and resource limits outrun defensive advantages.

global.name: Kolmanskop
global.summary: Kolmanskop buys time through remoteness and clear sightlines, but it cannot feed or hydrate a group for long. The dominant trade-off is safety from people versus total dependence on imported water and food.

global.name: Ligatne Bunker
global.summary: Ligatne's bunker geometry is excellent for sheltering, but what kills you here is air-power-water dependency: once life-support systems degrade, underground becomes a coffin.

global.name: Cheddar Gorge Caves
global.summary: Cheddar Gorge caves are a solid tactical hide with useful terrain friction; what kills you here is chronic livability failure, not direct assault.

global.name: Fort Copacabana
global.summary: Copacabana Fort is structurally robust and tactically defensible at the site level, but dense urban surroundings overwhelm long-term survivability.

global.name: Fastnet Lighthouse
global.summary: A remote offshore lighthouse with extreme separation and strong visibility. It is nearly useless as a survival base because space, shelter, food, water, and evacuation options are all critically limited.

global.name: Eguisheim
global.summary: Eguisheim is a workable village-scale fallback with manageable density and access to surrounding land. What kills you here is perimeter dilution once pressure exceeds what a small settlement can police.

global.name: Fort Denison
global.summary: A compact fortified island position with controllable access but almost no independent sustainment depth.

global.name: Naours Underground City
global.summary: Naours gives useful subterranean concealment and controlled entry, but it was never built as a full independent city. What kills you here is prolonged underground strain: air quality, hygiene, and supply depletion.

global.name: Utqiagvik
global.summary: Extreme remoteness sharply reduces contact risk, but Arctic dependence makes long survival brittle.

global.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
global.summary: The Great Mosque of Djenné is visually imposing and culturally significant, but materially fragile for sustained defensive use. It may serve as a symbolic shelter point, yet structural vulnerability and limited isolation make it unsuitable as a serious long-term survival base.

global.name: North Head Gun Emplacements
global.summary: North Head works as a hard defensive shell, but urban proximity and tiny sustainment depth make it a poor long-term base.

global.name: Kizhi Pogost
global.summary: Kizhi is remote and scenic, but what kills you here is infrastructure poverty: you run out of heat, medicine, and repair capacity before threats ever need to storm the site.

global.name: Phare du Créac'h
global.summary: Phare du Créac’h provides remote coastal isolation and observation value, but it is too small and brittle for extended habitation. What kills you here is capacity failure once stores run thin.

global.name: Uluru Surroundings
global.summary: Remote desert standoff lowers contact risk, but water and heat realities make it hard to sustain life.

africa.name: Aït Benhaddou
africa.summary: Aït Benhaddou is a strong niche base: its fortified settlement form and relative isolation support controlled defense and lower immediate pressure. Its long-term ceiling is set by arid constraints, where limited water and food capacity become the decisive bottleneck.

africa.name: Fasil Ghebbi
africa.summary: Fasil Ghebbi is a fortified royal compound with thick masonry, layered courtyards, and strong internal control, giving it above-average defensive potential in an inland setting. It is more balanced than many heritage landmarks, but long-term survival still depends on building reliable food, water, and medical systems beyond the walls.

africa.name: Table Mountain Plateau
africa.summary: Table Mountain Plateau is a highly defensible elevated position with steep cliffs, strong visibility, and usable space on top. However, its direct proximity to Cape Town, multiple access routes, and high visibility make it far less secure than more remote mountain strongholds. It is better suited to short-term defence and staging than long-term isolation.

africa.name: Elmina Castle
africa.summary: Elmina Castle is a heavily fortified coastal stronghold with thick walls, controlled internal spaces, and clear defensive advantages. However, its position within a populated coastal town and direct access from land and sea significantly reduce its long-term viability, making it better suited to temporary defence than sustained survival.

africa.name: Kimberley Big Hole & Mining Complex
africa.summary: The Kimberley Big Hole offers strong terrain-based defensibility, but it is a dangerous bowl if exits, water access, or supply routes fail. It works as a hard-to-storm holdout early on, yet can quickly become a trap once core lifelines are cut.

africa.name: Waw an Namus Cave System
africa.summary: Waw an Namus is one of the hardest places to reach, which dramatically lowers threat pressure. The same isolation becomes the fatal weakness because survival systems are almost entirely import-dependent.

africa.name: Kolmanskop
africa.summary: Kolmanskop buys time through remoteness and clear sightlines, but it cannot feed or hydrate a group for long. The dominant trade-off is safety from people versus total dependence on imported water and food.

africa.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
africa.summary: The Great Mosque of Djenné is visually imposing and culturally significant, but materially fragile for sustained defensive use. It may serve as a symbolic shelter point, yet structural vulnerability and limited isolation make it unsuitable as a serious long-term survival base.

east_asia.name: Jeju Island
east_asia.summary: Jeju is a strong island refuge with usable farmland, water access, and natural maritime separation from mainland spillover. What kills you here is maritime choke failure: if ports and fuel fail, an island-scale population can out-consume local capacity.

east_asia.name: Mount Huashan
east_asia.summary: Mount Huashan is an elite defensive perch with severe access control and strong natural isolation. The decisive trade-off is near-unmatched protection versus chronic logistical fragility.

east_asia.name: Iwo Jima Underground Bunkers
east_asia.summary: Iwo Jima’s bunker network is exceptionally hard to assault and highly isolated, but it is austere and resource-poor. What kills you here is life-support collapse underground: water, ventilation, and medical limits outrun defensive advantages.

east_asia.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge Cliffs
east_asia.summary: Tiger Leaping Gorge offers extraordinary terrain defense and low approach density, but daily survival is constrained by space and supply movement. The central trade-off is tactical dominance versus unworkable sustainment at scale.

east_asia.name: Himeji Castle
east_asia.summary: Himeji Castle delivers high-quality fortress geometry and controlled internal defense, but its urban context limits long-term security. The key trade-off is superb structure versus low isolation.

east_asia.name: Okinawa
east_asia.summary: Okinawa offers meaningful island separation and workable living conditions, but dense infrastructure and strategic visibility increase contest pressure. What kills you here is competition over ports, fuel, and transport hubs that fractures island stability.

east_asia.name: Shirakawa-go
east_asia.summary: Shirakawa-go benefits from mountain remoteness and small-settlement cohesion, but severe winters and limited redundancy constrain endurance. What kills you here is winter logistics failure: heat, medicine, and mobility collapse before threats do.

eastern_europe.name: Faroe Islands
eastern_europe.summary: Faroe is one of Europe's strongest isolation plays, but what kills you here is maritime bottleneck failure when storms, fuel limits, and fleet wear cut food and medical imports.

eastern_europe.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
eastern_europe.summary: Derinkuyu is an elite hide-and-hold refuge, but what kills you here is subterranean throughput collapse: ventilation, waste handling, and calorie flow fail before defenses do.

eastern_europe.name: Gotland
eastern_europe.summary: Gotland is a robust island option with workable infrastructure, but what kills you here is coastline overextension: too many access points for too few defenders over time.

eastern_europe.name: Malbork Castle
eastern_europe.summary: Malbork provides exceptional masonry defense and layered gates, but it sits in a reachable lowland region. What kills you here is siege attrition: repeated encirclement and supply disruption grind down even a strong fortress.

eastern_europe.name: Visby
eastern_europe.summary: Visby is a balanced walled island town, but what kills you here is population-and-water strain if too many survivors concentrate behind finite historic defenses.

eastern_europe.name: Predjama Castle
eastern_europe.summary: Predjama is a superb cliff fortress with choke-point control, but fortress geometry does not make food or medicine. What kills you here is siege starvation: you can deny entry for a long time and still lose to depletion.

eastern_europe.name: Suomenlinna Fortress
eastern_europe.summary: Suomenlinna has real island-fortress defensive logic, but it is tied to nearby urban waters and maritime supply. What kills you here is blockade-driven depletion when fuel, food, and treatment capacity cannot be replenished.

eastern_europe.name: Longyearbyen
eastern_europe.summary: A remote Arctic settlement with strong isolation, infrastructure, and controlled access. However, extreme climate and supply-chain reliance constrain long-term resilience.

eastern_europe.name: Ligatne Bunker
eastern_europe.summary: Ligatne's bunker geometry is excellent for sheltering, but what kills you here is air-power-water dependency: once life-support systems degrade, underground becomes a coffin.

eastern_europe.name: Kizhi Pogost
eastern_europe.summary: Kizhi is remote and scenic, but what kills you here is infrastructure poverty: you run out of heat, medicine, and repair capacity before threats ever need to storm the site.

middle_east.name: Socotra Island
middle_east.summary: Socotra gives outstanding separation from collapse corridors, but what kills you here is maritime supply fracture: once sea links fail, medicine, tools, and replacement goods run out faster than local systems can adapt.

middle_east.name: Krak des Chevaliers
middle_east.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a premier fortress for holding ground, but what kills you here is siege economics: ammunition, medicine, and calories run out long before the walls meaningfully fail.

middle_east.name: Cappadocia Highlands
middle_east.summary: Cappadocia’s broken terrain and concealment options make it a strong defensive refuge, but what kills you here is water-and-agriculture throughput: dispersed hideouts can outlast attacks, not prolonged scarcity.

middle_east.name: Siwa Oasis
middle_east.summary: Siwa Oasis is one of the more credible long-horizon refuges in the region, but what kills you here is water-system fragility: contamination, overdraw, or pump failure can collapse the settlement’s carrying capacity.

middle_east.name: Qeshm Island
middle_east.summary: Qeshm offers valuable island separation and room for mixed subsistence, but what kills you here is control dilution: the island is large enough that fragmented authority invites persistent infiltration and internal conflict.

middle_east.name: Masada
middle_east.summary: Masada is brutally hard to assault, but what kills you here is plateau logistics: water, heat management, and medical throughput collapse before attackers can force entry.

middle_east.name: Petra
middle_east.summary: Petra offers strong chokepoints and concealment in stone corridors, but what kills you here is water dependency: once stored supply and nearby sources are contested, defensive geometry cannot feed or hydrate a population.

middle_east.name: Al Udeid Air Base
middle_east.summary: Al Udeid provides one of the best ready-made defense envelopes in the region, but what kills you here is signature load: major airbase visibility attracts sustained external pressure and drains supplies.

north_america.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex
north_america.summary: Purpose-built hardened infrastructure makes this one of the most defensible options on the board.

north_america.name: Kodiak Island
north_america.summary: Kodiak is a high-isolation island with credible wild-resource potential, but its dominant failure mode is climate-logistics attrition: severe weather and seasonal bottlenecks steadily erode throughput, maintenance, and medical resilience.

north_america.name: Telluride
north_america.summary: Mountain terrain and manageable scale make Telluride a credible holdout if you prepare for winter logistics.

north_america.name: Alcatraz Island
north_america.summary: Alcatraz buys strong early security through water separation and choke-point access, but the decisive failure mode is supply starvation: once boat fuel, food inflow, and repair parts lapse, the island becomes a sealed deficit zone.

north_america.name: Mesa Verde
north_america.summary: Mesa Verde offers strong terrain defense, but what kills you here is carrying-capacity mismatch: protected positions can hold people, yet arable throughput and water logistics limit long-run population support.

north_america.name: Fort Jefferson
north_america.summary: Fort Jefferson is an exceptional sea-fortress with clear defensive geometry and extreme stand-off distance, but its dominant failure mode is water-energy fragility: if desalination and fuel chains degrade, habitability collapses quickly.

north_america.name: Guantanamo Bay
north_america.summary: Guantanamo offers strong perimeter control and organized facilities, yet the dominant failure mode is geopolitical encirclement: prolonged dependence on maritime logistics and contested sovereignty can choke continuity even before direct breach.

north_america.name: Table Rock Plateau
north_america.summary: Table Rock is a serviceable elevated fallback, but what kills you here is perimeter dilution: broad approach arcs and limited concealment stretch defenders until incidents become constant.

north_america.name: Hutchinson Salt Storage Caverns
north_america.summary: Hutchinson salt caverns provide excellent blast/weather protection and concealment, yet the single dominant failure mode is ventilation-power dependency: lose airflow and pumping reliability, and the underground advantage becomes a liability.

north_america.name: Utqiagvik
north_america.summary: Extreme remoteness sharply reduces contact risk, but Arctic dependence makes long survival brittle.

oceania.name: Tasmania
oceania.summary: Tasmania is one of the strongest balanced options: durable food-water-energy potential with enough separation to reduce pressure.

oceania.name: Fiji Islands
oceania.summary: Fiji balances isolation and livability better than most island options, but cyclone and maritime dependence cap reliability.

oceania.name: Coober Pedy Underground Settlement
oceania.summary: Coober Pedy is one of the few desert sites where underground habitation is already proven, but long-term success is limited by hard water and logistics ceilings.

oceania.name: Pine Gap Facility
oceania.summary: Extreme remoteness and hardened controls are offset by acute system dependency and top-tier strategic exposure.

oceania.name: Blue Mountains Cliffs
oceania.summary: Excellent terrain defense and standoff distance, with sustainment limited by wildfire and infrastructure thinness.

oceania.name: Fort Denison
oceania.summary: A compact fortified island position with controllable access but almost no independent sustainment depth.

oceania.name: North Head Gun Emplacements
oceania.summary: North Head works as a hard defensive shell, but urban proximity and tiny sustainment depth make it a poor long-term base.

oceania.name: Uluru Surroundings
oceania.summary: Remote desert standoff lowers contact risk, but water and heat realities make it hard to sustain life.

polar_extreme.name: Olavsvern Naval Base
polar_extreme.summary: A hardened underground naval base with strong concealment and protected infrastructure. However, confined systems, external supply needs, and limited scalability restrict long-term survival.

polar_extreme.name: Nagurskoye Air Base
polar_extreme.summary: A remote Arctic military airbase with controlled access and strong strategic positioning. However, extreme climate, visibility, and dependence on supply chains reduce independent survivability.

polar_extreme.name: McMurdo Station
polar_extreme.summary: A large Antarctic research station with infrastructure, shelter, and operational capacity. However, harsh conditions and dependence on supply chains limit true long-term independence.

polar_extreme.name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
polar_extreme.summary: An extremely isolated scientific station with controlled infrastructure and almost no external threat pressure. However, total dependence on life-support systems and resupply makes long-term independence impossible.

polar_extreme.name: Camp Century Ice Tunnels
polar_extreme.summary: Camp Century is exceptionally hard to reach and hard to assault, but it fails as a settlement because the environment itself destroys long-term habitability.

south_america.name: Chiloé Island
south_america.summary: Chiloé is a strong all-round island base with workable agriculture and defensible approaches, but what kills you here is prolonged maritime cutoff during a hard winter.

south_america.name: Cusco Highlands Village
south_america.summary: Cusco highlands villages combine terrain defense with proven local subsistence systems, but what kills you here is cold-altitude medical decline in unacclimated groups.

south_america.name: Machu Picchu
south_america.summary: Machu Picchu offers excellent terrain defense and controlled approach lines, but limited productive capacity prevents large, permanent survival communities.

south_america.name: Galápagos Islands
south_america.summary: Galápagos has extreme isolation and low random threat traffic, but what kills you here is supply collapse once imported essentials stop.

south_america.name: San Felipe Fortress
south_america.summary: San Felipe combines historical fortification advantages with moderate operating feasibility, but limited local throughput caps long-term resilience.

south_america.name: Amazon Tall Tower Observatory
south_america.summary: ATTO offers deep-rainforest isolation and strong natural resource potential, but terrain, disease burden, and mobility constraints make control and continuity difficult.

south_america.name: Tambopata Research Center
south_america.summary: Tambopata gives concealment and food potential in deep jungle, but what kills you here is untreated injury or infection far from reliable care.

south_america.name: Fort Copacabana
south_america.summary: Copacabana Fort is structurally robust and tactically defensible at the site level, but dense urban surroundings overwhelm long-term survivability.

south_asia.name: Andaman Islands
south_asia.summary: The Andamans are one of the strongest long-horizon options: maritime isolation and resource diversity create resilience if governance and inter-island logistics stay coherent.

south_asia.name: Mehrangarh Fort
south_asia.summary: Mehrangarh combines exceptional fortification geometry with workable internal scale, making it one of the stronger fortress options if surrounding pressure is actively managed.

south_asia.name: Hilltop Fort Rajasthan
south_asia.summary: A Rajasthan hill fort is a classic high-control stronghold with excellent wall geometry, but water and heat stress define whether it thrives or slowly fails.

south_asia.name: Sigiriya
south_asia.summary: Sigiriya offers rare rock-fortress defensibility and visibility, but constrained top-plateau capacity limits how long a group can live there without strong external support.

south_asia.name: Hanle Observatory
south_asia.summary: Hanle Observatory is an isolation-dominant survival option with low encounter pressure, but extreme altitude and remoteness impose severe physiological and logistics penalties.

south_asia.name: Kargil War Bunkers
south_asia.summary: Kargil War Bunkers are military-hardened high-altitude positions designed to resist assault. They work by combining strong fortification with terrain that channels approaches. You die when cold-weather fuel, medical, and resupply throughput collapses before defenses do.

south_asia.name: Tiger’s Nest Monastery
south_asia.summary: Tiger’s Nest is an extreme cliffside redoubt with elite access denial, but its tiny carrying capacity and severe logistics ceiling cap long-term survival.

south_asia.name: Kibber Village
south_asia.summary: Kibber is a high-altitude remote village that trades accessibility for security. It works through isolation, narrow approaches, and existing community housing for organized routines. You die when winter isolation, fuel gaps, or delayed medical care compound faster than recovery.

south_asia.name: Lakshadweep
south_asia.summary: Lakshadweep is a distributed island-chain refuge where sea separation reduces routine contact and gives strong early warning. It works when multiple islands coordinate boats, storage, and rationing as one system. You die when maritime links or freshwater discipline fail and each island is stranded alone.

south_asia.name: Ajanta Caves
south_asia.summary: Ajanta Caves are a hardened cave shelter system with strong choke-point defense. It works for short protected occupancy because rock-cut access geometry lowers breach risk. You die when confinement-driven sanitation and resource limits outrun defensive advantages.

southeast_asia.name: Palawan
southeast_asia.summary: Palawan is a large island system that balances isolation, defensibility, and resource diversity. It works when distributed settlements and logistics are coordinated at island-wide scale. You die when governance fractures and shipping disruption desynchronizes regional supply.

southeast_asia.name: Rice Terrace Highlands
southeast_asia.summary: Rice Terrace Highlands are elevated agrarian settlements with built-in food potential. They work by combining controllable approach routes with reliable staple production systems. You die when irrigation, labor coordination, or slope access fails during stress cycles.

southeast_asia.name: Banda Neira
southeast_asia.summary: A small island settlement with strong maritime separation, historic fortifications, and access to coastal resources. It works best as a low-profile island refuge, but limited scale and supply dependence cap long-term resilience.

southeast_asia.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
southeast_asia.summary: A purpose-built tunnel network with concealment, restricted access, and strong defensive history. It is highly effective for short-term evasion, but confinement, ventilation, and resource limits make permanent survival difficult.

southeast_asia.name: Ha Long Bay Cliffs
southeast_asia.summary: Ha Long Bay cliffs are a terrain-fragmented coastal redoubt of islands and vertical rock. It works by forcing movement through predictable maritime channels and narrow landing points. You die when weather or boat degradation cuts mobility and resupply between sectors.

southeast_asia.name: Hue Citadel
southeast_asia.summary: Hue Citadel is a fortified urban compound with layered walls and controlled gates. It works as a short-to-medium defensive enclave where geometry slows penetration. You die when siege pressure outlasts external food, fuel, and medical inflows.

southeast_asia.name: Komodo Island
southeast_asia.summary: Komodo is a highly isolated island refuge with strong separation from mainland pressure. It works by limiting approach routes and maintaining disciplined low-population maritime living. You die when freshwater constraints and sea-logistics disruption trigger cascading shortages.

southeast_asia.name: Danum Valley Field Centre
southeast_asia.summary: Danum Valley Field Centre is a remote jungle refuge with low-contact signature advantages. It works for small trained groups that can run strict field medicine and maintenance routines. You die when treatable illness, injury, or equipment failure outpaces evacuation and repair.

southeast_asia.name: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base
southeast_asia.summary: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base is a military command compound with strong tactical security. It works through hardened access control, organized response, and maritime support infrastructure. You die when prolonged contest burns fuel, parts, and readiness faster than resupply.

southeast_asia.name: Banlung
southeast_asia.summary: A remote inland town with surrounding terrain, forest cover, and regional resource access. It offers more livability than a pure wilderness refuge, but weak defensibility and difficult logistics limit its ceiling.

uk_ireland.name: Isle of Eigg Village
uk_ireland.summary: A rare location that is both naturally isolated and genuinely capable of long-term habitation. Eigg is less a fortress than a sustainable island community: survival depends on protecting a small, disciplined population and refusing growth beyond the island's natural carrying capacity.

uk_ireland.name: Burlington Bunker
uk_ireland.summary: Burlington is exceptionally hard to breach in the opening phase; what kills you here is closed-system decay once consumables, maintenance, or governance slip.

uk_ireland.name: Lindisfarne
uk_ireland.summary: A tidal island with natural separation, limited access windows, and a defensible settlement pattern. It works well for a disciplined small group, but tide dependency and resource limits cap long-term resilience.

uk_ireland.name: Caerphilly Castle
uk_ireland.summary: A large moated castle with strong defensive design and layered barriers. It is one of the stronger historic fortifications, but modern exposure and limited self-sufficiency keep it from elite status.

uk_ireland.name: St Kilda
uk_ireland.summary: An extremely remote island archipelago with exceptional isolation and low external threat pressure. Its weakness is sustainment: weather, landing difficulty, and limited resources make survival fragile over time.

uk_ireland.name: Fort George
uk_ireland.summary: A purpose-built coastal military fort with strong walls, controlled access, and organised internal space. It has real defensive value, but exposure and reliance on external supplies limit long-term independence.

uk_ireland.name: HM Prison Dartmoor
uk_ireland.summary: A remote prison complex with secure walls, controlled movement, and strong internal containment. It offers a credible short-term defensive shell, but harsh exposure and limited self-sufficiency constrain long-term survival.

uk_ireland.name: Clovelly
uk_ireland.summary: A steep coastal village with constrained access routes, natural defensibility, and small-scale shelter. It is viable as a compact refuge, but limited expansion, coastal exposure, and supply dependence restrict long-term survival.

uk_ireland.name: Edinburgh Castle
uk_ireland.summary: A highly defensible urban castle on elevated rock, with strong visibility and controlled approaches. It is excellent as a symbolic redoubt, but urban exposure and limited sustainability reduce long-term value.

uk_ireland.name: The Roaches
uk_ireland.summary: A rocky elevated ridge with natural defensibility, visibility, and difficult approaches. It works as a temporary fallback point, but exposure and lack of infrastructure make it unsuitable for long-term occupation.

uk_ireland.name: Cheddar Gorge Caves
uk_ireland.summary: Cheddar Gorge caves are a solid tactical hide with useful terrain friction; what kills you here is chronic livability failure, not direct assault.

uk_ireland.name: Fastnet Lighthouse
uk_ireland.summary: A remote offshore lighthouse with extreme separation and strong visibility. It is nearly useless as a survival base because space, shelter, food, water, and evacuation options are all critically limited.

western_europe.name: Heligoland
western_europe.summary: Heligoland is one of the strongest isolation plays in Western Europe: remote, compact, and easier to monitor than mainland sites. What kills you here is maritime dependency when weather or fuel cuts the lifeline.

western_europe.name: Mont Saint-Michel
western_europe.summary: Mont Saint-Michel is arguably one of Europe’s strongest defensive positions: a tidal island with medieval walls, steep approaches, elevated fighting positions, and commanding visibility across the bay. Its real survival test is not whether zombies can storm the mount; it is whether the people inside can solve food, freshwater, and crowd-control problems once mainland supply chains fail.

western_europe.name: Carcassonne
western_europe.summary: Carcassonne is a premier fortified shell with layered walls and command depth; what kills you here is sustainment fatigue behind intact defenses.

western_europe.name: Hallstatt
western_europe.summary: Hallstatt combines constrained access with strong local livability, making it one of the better balanced settlement options. What kills you here is chokepoint failure that traps residents against terrain.

western_europe.name: Île d’Yeu
western_europe.summary: Île d’Yeu is a balanced island refuge with useful separation and livable conditions, but it lacks deep strategic depth. What kills you here is slow resource depletion under prolonged isolation.

western_europe.name: Rocamadour
western_europe.summary: Rocamadour balances cliffside defense with workable rural linkage; what kills you here is exceeding carrying capacity and overloading water/sanitation systems.

western_europe.name: Maginot Line Bunkers
western_europe.summary: The Maginot bunkers are elite for hard protection but poor at independent endurance. What kills you here is subsystem failure underground: air, water, power, and sanitation.

western_europe.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
western_europe.summary: Neuschwanstein offers strong terrain-assisted defense and visibility; what kills you here is logistics drag from a symbolic site that cannot feed itself.

western_europe.name: Eguisheim
western_europe.summary: Eguisheim is a workable village-scale fallback with manageable density and access to surrounding land. What kills you here is perimeter dilution once pressure exceeds what a small settlement can police.

western_europe.name: Naours Underground City
western_europe.summary: Naours gives useful subterranean concealment and controlled entry, but it was never built as a full independent city. What kills you here is prolonged underground strain: air quality, hygiene, and supply depletion.

western_europe.name: Phare du Créac'h
western_europe.summary: Phare du Créac’h provides remote coastal isolation and observation value, but it is too small and brittle for extended habitation. What kills you here is capacity failure once stores run thin.

elevated_stronghold.name: Machu Picchu
elevated_stronghold.summary: Machu Picchu offers excellent terrain defense and controlled approach lines, but limited productive capacity prevents large, permanent survival communities.

elevated_stronghold.name: Simien Mountains
elevated_stronghold.summary: The Simien Mountains are a naturally defensible high-altitude stronghold, where sheer cliffs, limited access routes, and extreme isolation significantly reduce external threat pressure. However, that same isolation severely limits long-term survivability, with constrained food production, harsh living conditions, and difficult resupply. Over time, the balance shifts from protection to restriction, making it better suited to short-term refuge than permanent settlement.

fortified_structure.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a premier fortress for holding ground, but what kills you here is siege economics: ammunition, medicine, and calories run out long before the walls meaningfully fail.

fortified_structure.name: Malbork Castle
fortified_structure.summary: Malbork provides exceptional masonry defense and layered gates, but it sits in a reachable lowland region. What kills you here is siege attrition: repeated encirclement and supply disruption grind down even a strong fortress.

fortified_structure.name: Fasil Ghebbi
fortified_structure.summary: Fasil Ghebbi is a fortified royal compound with thick masonry, layered courtyards, and strong internal control, giving it above-average defensive potential in an inland setting. It is more balanced than many heritage landmarks, but long-term survival still depends on building reliable food, water, and medical systems beyond the walls.

fortified_structure.name: Alcatraz Island
fortified_structure.summary: Alcatraz buys strong early security through water separation and choke-point access, but the decisive failure mode is supply starvation: once boat fuel, food inflow, and repair parts lapse, the island becomes a sealed deficit zone.

fortified_structure.name: Caerphilly Castle
fortified_structure.summary: A large moated castle with strong defensive design and layered barriers. It is one of the stronger historic fortifications, but modern exposure and limited self-sufficiency keep it from elite status.

fortified_structure.name: Himeji Castle
fortified_structure.summary: Himeji Castle delivers high-quality fortress geometry and controlled internal defense, but its urban context limits long-term security. The key trade-off is superb structure versus low isolation.

fortified_structure.name: Masada
fortified_structure.summary: Masada is brutally hard to assault, but what kills you here is plateau logistics: water, heat management, and medical throughput collapse before attackers can force entry.

fortified_structure.name: Fort George
fortified_structure.summary: A purpose-built coastal military fort with strong walls, controlled access, and organised internal space. It has real defensive value, but exposure and reliance on external supplies limit long-term independence.

fortified_structure.name: Fort Jefferson
fortified_structure.summary: Fort Jefferson is an exceptional sea-fortress with clear defensive geometry and extreme stand-off distance, but its dominant failure mode is water-energy fragility: if desalination and fuel chains degrade, habitability collapses quickly.

fortified_structure.name: Hue Citadel
fortified_structure.summary: Hue Citadel is a fortified urban compound with layered walls and controlled gates. It works as a short-to-medium defensive enclave where geometry slows penetration. You die when siege pressure outlasts external food, fuel, and medical inflows.

fortified_structure.name: Suomenlinna Fortress
fortified_structure.summary: Suomenlinna has real island-fortress defensive logic, but it is tied to nearby urban waters and maritime supply. What kills you here is blockade-driven depletion when fuel, food, and treatment capacity cannot be replenished.

fortified_structure.name: McMurdo Station
fortified_structure.summary: A large Antarctic research station with infrastructure, shelter, and operational capacity. However, harsh conditions and dependence on supply chains limit true long-term independence.

fortified_structure.name: San Felipe Fortress
fortified_structure.summary: San Felipe combines historical fortification advantages with moderate operating feasibility, but limited local throughput caps long-term resilience.

fortified_structure.name: Elmina Castle
fortified_structure.summary: Elmina Castle is a heavily fortified coastal stronghold with thick walls, controlled internal spaces, and clear defensive advantages. However, its position within a populated coastal town and direct access from land and sea significantly reduce its long-term viability, making it better suited to temporary defence than sustained survival.

fortified_structure.name: Fort Copacabana
fortified_structure.summary: Copacabana Fort is structurally robust and tactically defensible at the site level, but dense urban surroundings overwhelm long-term survivability.

fortified_structure.name: Fort Denison
fortified_structure.summary: A compact fortified island position with controllable access but almost no independent sustainment depth.

industrial_site.name: Kimberley Big Hole & Mining Complex
industrial_site.summary: The Kimberley Big Hole offers strong terrain-based defensibility, but it is a dangerous bowl if exits, water access, or supply routes fail. It works as a hard-to-storm holdout early on, yet can quickly become a trap once core lifelines are cut.

industrial_site.name: Hutchinson Salt Storage Caverns
industrial_site.summary: Hutchinson salt caverns provide excellent blast/weather protection and concealment, yet the single dominant failure mode is ventilation-power dependency: lose airflow and pumping reliability, and the underground advantage becomes a liability.

institutional_compound.name: Hanle Observatory
institutional_compound.summary: Hanle Observatory is an isolation-dominant survival option with low encounter pressure, but extreme altitude and remoteness impose severe physiological and logistics penalties.

institutional_compound.name: Nagurskoye Air Base
institutional_compound.summary: A remote Arctic military airbase with controlled access and strong strategic positioning. However, extreme climate, visibility, and dependence on supply chains reduce independent survivability.

institutional_compound.name: HM Prison Dartmoor
institutional_compound.summary: A remote prison complex with secure walls, controlled movement, and strong internal containment. It offers a credible short-term defensive shell, but harsh exposure and limited self-sufficiency constrain long-term survival.

institutional_compound.name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
institutional_compound.summary: An extremely isolated scientific station with controlled infrastructure and almost no external threat pressure. However, total dependence on life-support systems and resupply makes long-term independence impossible.

institutional_compound.name: Danum Valley Field Centre
institutional_compound.summary: Danum Valley Field Centre is a remote jungle refuge with low-contact signature advantages. It works for small trained groups that can run strict field medicine and maintenance routines. You die when treatable illness, injury, or equipment failure outpaces evacuation and repair.

institutional_compound.name: Pine Gap Facility
institutional_compound.summary: Extreme remoteness and hardened controls are offset by acute system dependency and top-tier strategic exposure.

institutional_compound.name: Al Udeid Air Base
institutional_compound.summary: Al Udeid provides one of the best ready-made defense envelopes in the region, but what kills you here is signature load: major airbase visibility attracts sustained external pressure and drains supplies.

institutional_compound.name: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base
institutional_compound.summary: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base is a military command compound with strong tactical security. It works through hardened access control, organized response, and maritime support infrastructure. You die when prolonged contest burns fuel, parts, and readiness faster than resupply.

institutional_compound.name: Amazon Tall Tower Observatory
institutional_compound.summary: ATTO offers deep-rainforest isolation and strong natural resource potential, but terrain, disease burden, and mobility constraints make control and continuity difficult.

institutional_compound.name: Guantanamo Bay
institutional_compound.summary: Guantanamo offers strong perimeter control and organized facilities, yet the dominant failure mode is geopolitical encirclement: prolonged dependence on maritime logistics and contested sovereignty can choke continuity even before direct breach.

institutional_compound.name: Tambopata Research Center
institutional_compound.summary: Tambopata gives concealment and food potential in deep jungle, but what kills you here is untreated injury or infection far from reliable care.

isolated_landmass.name: Andaman Islands
isolated_landmass.summary: The Andamans are one of the strongest long-horizon options: maritime isolation and resource diversity create resilience if governance and inter-island logistics stay coherent.

isolated_landmass.name: Tasmania
isolated_landmass.summary: Tasmania is one of the strongest balanced options: durable food-water-energy potential with enough separation to reduce pressure.

isolated_landmass.name: Chiloé Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Chiloé is a strong all-round island base with workable agriculture and defensible approaches, but what kills you here is prolonged maritime cutoff during a hard winter.

isolated_landmass.name: Heligoland
isolated_landmass.summary: Heligoland is one of the strongest isolation plays in Western Europe: remote, compact, and easier to monitor than mainland sites. What kills you here is maritime dependency when weather or fuel cuts the lifeline.

isolated_landmass.name: Seychelles
isolated_landmass.summary: Seychelles is one of the strongest African macro-base options because exceptional island isolation combines with a livable climate and realistic long-term habitation potential. The main constraint is coordination and resupply across dispersed islands once external systems weaken.

isolated_landmass.name: Faroe Islands
isolated_landmass.summary: Faroe is one of Europe's strongest isolation plays, but what kills you here is maritime bottleneck failure when storms, fuel limits, and fleet wear cut food and medical imports.

isolated_landmass.name: Socotra Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Socotra gives outstanding separation from collapse corridors, but what kills you here is maritime supply fracture: once sea links fail, medicine, tools, and replacement goods run out faster than local systems can adapt.

isolated_landmass.name: Fiji Islands
isolated_landmass.summary: Fiji balances isolation and livability better than most island options, but cyclone and maritime dependence cap reliability.

isolated_landmass.name: Palawan
isolated_landmass.summary: Palawan is a large island system that balances isolation, defensibility, and resource diversity. It works when distributed settlements and logistics are coordinated at island-wide scale. You die when governance fractures and shipping disruption desynchronizes regional supply.

isolated_landmass.name: Kodiak Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Kodiak is a high-isolation island with credible wild-resource potential, but its dominant failure mode is climate-logistics attrition: severe weather and seasonal bottlenecks steadily erode throughput, maintenance, and medical resilience.

isolated_landmass.name: Zanzibar Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Zanzibar balances meaningful island separation with established settlement infrastructure, making it a credible medium-to-long-term refuge if governance and resource management remain coherent. Its challenge is that it is populated and close enough to mainland dynamics to face persistent pressure.

isolated_landmass.name: Gotland
isolated_landmass.summary: Gotland is a robust island option with workable infrastructure, but what kills you here is coastline overextension: too many access points for too few defenders over time.

isolated_landmass.name: Jeju Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Jeju is a strong island refuge with usable farmland, water access, and natural maritime separation from mainland spillover. What kills you here is maritime choke failure: if ports and fuel fail, an island-scale population can out-consume local capacity.

isolated_landmass.name: Galápagos Islands
isolated_landmass.summary: Galápagos has extreme isolation and low random threat traffic, but what kills you here is supply collapse once imported essentials stop.

isolated_landmass.name: Île d’Yeu
isolated_landmass.summary: Île d’Yeu is a balanced island refuge with useful separation and livable conditions, but it lacks deep strategic depth. What kills you here is slow resource depletion under prolonged isolation.

isolated_landmass.name: Lindisfarne
isolated_landmass.summary: A tidal island with natural separation, limited access windows, and a defensible settlement pattern. It works well for a disciplined small group, but tide dependency and resource limits cap long-term resilience.

isolated_landmass.name: Qeshm Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Qeshm offers valuable island separation and room for mixed subsistence, but what kills you here is control dilution: the island is large enough that fragmented authority invites persistent infiltration and internal conflict.

isolated_landmass.name: St Kilda
isolated_landmass.summary: An extremely remote island archipelago with exceptional isolation and low external threat pressure. Its weakness is sustainment: weather, landing difficulty, and limited resources make survival fragile over time.

isolated_landmass.name: Komodo Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Komodo is a highly isolated island refuge with strong separation from mainland pressure. It works by limiting approach routes and maintaining disciplined low-population maritime living. You die when freshwater constraints and sea-logistics disruption trigger cascading shortages.

isolated_landmass.name: Lakshadweep
isolated_landmass.summary: Lakshadweep is a distributed island-chain refuge where sea separation reduces routine contact and gives strong early warning. It works when multiple islands coordinate boats, storage, and rationing as one system. You die when maritime links or freshwater discipline fail and each island is stranded alone.

isolated_landmass.name: Okinawa
isolated_landmass.summary: Okinawa offers meaningful island separation and workable living conditions, but dense infrastructure and strategic visibility increase contest pressure. What kills you here is competition over ports, fuel, and transport hubs that fractures island stability.

landmark_structure.name: Fastnet Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: A remote offshore lighthouse with extreme separation and strong visibility. It is nearly useless as a survival base because space, shelter, food, water, and evacuation options are all critically limited.

landmark_structure.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
landmark_structure.summary: The Great Mosque of Djenné is visually imposing and culturally significant, but materially fragile for sustained defensive use. It may serve as a symbolic shelter point, yet structural vulnerability and limited isolation make it unsuitable as a serious long-term survival base.

landmark_structure.name: Kizhi Pogost
landmark_structure.summary: Kizhi is remote and scenic, but what kills you here is infrastructure poverty: you run out of heat, medicine, and repair capacity before threats ever need to storm the site.

landmark_structure.name: Phare du Créac'h
landmark_structure.summary: Phare du Créac’h provides remote coastal isolation and observation value, but it is too small and brittle for extended habitation. What kills you here is capacity failure once stores run thin.

remote_settlement.name: Isle of Eigg Village
remote_settlement.summary: A rare location that is both naturally isolated and genuinely capable of long-term habitation. Eigg is less a fortress than a sustainable island community: survival depends on protecting a small, disciplined population and refusing growth beyond the island's natural carrying capacity.

remote_settlement.name: Cusco Highlands Village
remote_settlement.summary: Cusco highlands villages combine terrain defense with proven local subsistence systems, but what kills you here is cold-altitude medical decline in unacclimated groups.

remote_settlement.name: Coober Pedy Underground Settlement
remote_settlement.summary: Coober Pedy is one of the few desert sites where underground habitation is already proven, but long-term success is limited by hard water and logistics ceilings.

remote_settlement.name: Siwa Oasis
remote_settlement.summary: Siwa Oasis is one of the more credible long-horizon refuges in the region, but what kills you here is water-system fragility: contamination, overdraw, or pump failure can collapse the settlement’s carrying capacity.

remote_settlement.name: Aït Benhaddou
remote_settlement.summary: Aït Benhaddou is a strong niche base: its fortified settlement form and relative isolation support controlled defense and lower immediate pressure. Its long-term ceiling is set by arid constraints, where limited water and food capacity become the decisive bottleneck.

remote_settlement.name: Hallstatt
remote_settlement.summary: Hallstatt combines constrained access with strong local livability, making it one of the better balanced settlement options. What kills you here is chokepoint failure that traps residents against terrain.

remote_settlement.name: Telluride
remote_settlement.summary: Mountain terrain and manageable scale make Telluride a credible holdout if you prepare for winter logistics.

remote_settlement.name: Visby
remote_settlement.summary: Visby is a balanced walled island town, but what kills you here is population-and-water strain if too many survivors concentrate behind finite historic defenses.

remote_settlement.name: Banda Neira
remote_settlement.summary: A small island settlement with strong maritime separation, historic fortifications, and access to coastal resources. It works best as a low-profile island refuge, but limited scale and supply dependence cap long-term resilience.

remote_settlement.name: Clovelly
remote_settlement.summary: A steep coastal village with constrained access routes, natural defensibility, and small-scale shelter. It is viable as a compact refuge, but limited expansion, coastal exposure, and supply dependence restrict long-term survival.

remote_settlement.name: Kibber Village
remote_settlement.summary: Kibber is a high-altitude remote village that trades accessibility for security. It works through isolation, narrow approaches, and existing community housing for organized routines. You die when winter isolation, fuel gaps, or delayed medical care compound faster than recovery.

remote_settlement.name: Longyearbyen
remote_settlement.summary: A remote Arctic settlement with strong isolation, infrastructure, and controlled access. However, extreme climate and supply-chain reliance constrain long-term resilience.

remote_settlement.name: Banlung
remote_settlement.summary: A remote inland town with surrounding terrain, forest cover, and regional resource access. It offers more livability than a pure wilderness refuge, but weak defensibility and difficult logistics limit its ceiling.

remote_settlement.name: Shirakawa-go
remote_settlement.summary: Shirakawa-go benefits from mountain remoteness and small-settlement cohesion, but severe winters and limited redundancy constrain endurance. What kills you here is winter logistics failure: heat, medicine, and mobility collapse before threats do.

remote_settlement.name: Kolmanskop
remote_settlement.summary: Kolmanskop buys time through remoteness and clear sightlines, but it cannot feed or hydrate a group for long. The dominant trade-off is safety from people versus total dependence on imported water and food.

remote_settlement.name: Eguisheim
remote_settlement.summary: Eguisheim is a workable village-scale fallback with manageable density and access to surrounding land. What kills you here is perimeter dilution once pressure exceeds what a small settlement can police.

remote_settlement.name: Utqiagvik
remote_settlement.summary: Extreme remoteness sharply reduces contact risk, but Arctic dependence makes long survival brittle.

subterranean.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex
subterranean.summary: Purpose-built hardened infrastructure makes this one of the most defensible options on the board.

subterranean.name: Matmata Underground Dwellings
subterranean.summary: Matmata offers a strong concealment-defense package with naturally insulated subterranean housing and manageable access points. Its core trade-off is protected living space versus limited scale and external dependence for growth.

subterranean.name: Burlington Bunker
subterranean.summary: Burlington is exceptionally hard to breach in the opening phase; what kills you here is closed-system decay once consumables, maintenance, or governance slip.

subterranean.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
subterranean.summary: Derinkuyu is an elite hide-and-hold refuge, but what kills you here is subterranean throughput collapse: ventilation, waste handling, and calorie flow fail before defenses do.

subterranean.name: Kargil War Bunkers
subterranean.summary: Kargil War Bunkers are military-hardened high-altitude positions designed to resist assault. They work by combining strong fortification with terrain that channels approaches. You die when cold-weather fuel, medical, and resupply throughput collapses before defenses do.

subterranean.name: Iwo Jima Underground Bunkers
subterranean.summary: Iwo Jima’s bunker network is exceptionally hard to assault and highly isolated, but it is austere and resource-poor. What kills you here is life-support collapse underground: water, ventilation, and medical limits outrun defensive advantages.

subterranean.name: Olavsvern Naval Base
subterranean.summary: A hardened underground naval base with strong concealment and protected infrastructure. However, confined systems, external supply needs, and limited scalability restrict long-term survival.

subterranean.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
subterranean.summary: A purpose-built tunnel network with concealment, restricted access, and strong defensive history. It is highly effective for short-term evasion, but confinement, ventilation, and resource limits make permanent survival difficult.

subterranean.name: Maginot Line Bunkers
subterranean.summary: The Maginot bunkers are elite for hard protection but poor at independent endurance. What kills you here is subsystem failure underground: air, water, power, and sanitation.

subterranean.name: Camp Century Ice Tunnels
subterranean.summary: Camp Century is exceptionally hard to reach and hard to assault, but it fails as a settlement because the environment itself destroys long-term habitability.

subterranean.name: Waw an Namus Cave System
subterranean.summary: Waw an Namus is one of the hardest places to reach, which dramatically lowers threat pressure. The same isolation becomes the fatal weakness because survival systems are almost entirely import-dependent.

subterranean.name: Ajanta Caves
subterranean.summary: Ajanta Caves are a hardened cave shelter system with strong choke-point defense. It works for short protected occupancy because rock-cut access geometry lowers breach risk. You die when confinement-driven sanitation and resource limits outrun defensive advantages.

subterranean.name: Ligatne Bunker
subterranean.summary: Ligatne's bunker geometry is excellent for sheltering, but what kills you here is air-power-water dependency: once life-support systems degrade, underground becomes a coffin.

subterranean.name: Cheddar Gorge Caves
subterranean.summary: Cheddar Gorge caves are a solid tactical hide with useful terrain friction; what kills you here is chronic livability failure, not direct assault.

subterranean.name: Naours Underground City
subterranean.summary: Naours gives useful subterranean concealment and controlled entry, but it was never built as a full independent city. What kills you here is prolonged underground strain: air quality, hygiene, and supply depletion.

subterranean.name: North Head Gun Emplacements
subterranean.summary: North Head works as a hard defensive shell, but urban proximity and tiny sustainment depth make it a poor long-term base.
